name: Ford Performance Vehicles (FPV)
overview: Ford Performance Vehicles (FPV) was established in 2002 in Campbellfield, Victoria as a high-performance joint venture between Ford Australia and British racing powerhouse Prodrive, succeeding Tickford Vehicle Engineering (TVE). FPV engineered the most devastating performance Falcons ever created. FPV became renowned for its hand-assembled 'Boss' quad-cam 32-valve 5.4-litre V8s (Boss 290, 302, 315) and the revolutionary turbocharged 'Barra' 4.0-litre twin-cam six in the F6 Typhoon and Tornado (yielding a massive 565Nm of torque). In 2010, FPV introduced the Australian-developed 'Miami' 5.0-litre supercharged V8, crowning its legacy with the limited-edition 2014 FG GT-F 351 (capable of over 400kW on overboost), before operations concluded in late 2014.
australian_history:
FPV was born from the rich heritage of Tickford Vehicle Engineering (TVE), established in 1991 to create the Falcon XR6 and XR8. In 2002, Ford and Prodrive established Ford Performance Vehicles at Campbellfield, directly opposite Ford's main plant. Under chief engineer Bryan Mears and Prodrive boss David Flint, FPV launched the BA GT and GT-P in early 2003, featuring the Boss 290—a unique Australian creation pairing an American modular 5.4L cast-iron block with quad-cam 32-valve cylinder heads from the Mustang Cobra R.

In late 2004, FPV launched the F6 Typhoon sedan and F6 Tornado ute, powered by a high-boost version of the Barra 4.0-litre inline-six developing 270kW and 550Nm of torque. The F6 out-accelerated contemporary V8s and earned legendary status as one of Australia's greatest performance engines.

In 2008, the FG series introduced the Boss 315 V8 and the F6 310 (310kW/565Nm) featuring an enormous front-mount intercooler and Garrett GT3576R turbocharger. In late 2010, under 'Project Panther', FPV invested $40 million to develop the supercharged 'Miami' 5.0-litre V8 based on Ford's Coyote engine, incorporating a top-mounted Harrop HTV 1900 supercharger with integrated water-to-air intercooling. In 2012, Ford bought out Prodrive's stake in FPV, integrating production directly into Ford Broadmeadows. FPV signed off in June 2014 with the GT-F 351 (351kW / 570Nm, paying tribute to the 351 Cleveland), with 500 numbered sedans built for Australia.
